documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit from her car in the school lot, identity verified.

33F G4P3 at 20w3d. Here for the mid-pregnancy iron check we planned. OB visits on schedule, nothing new from them. Taking levothyroxine on waking, iron at night, prenatal daily. No dizziness, no bleeding.

Hx relevant: PPH x2 (2023 atony/home birth, transfused 2u; 2024 vaginal wall laceration, OR repair). OB planning hospital delivery with hemorrhage precautions.

Exam (video): well appearing, speaking comfortably, no distress.

A/P
- Iron deficiency anemia in pregnancy: CBC + iron studies tomorrow. Continue ferrous sulfate. Results to OB.
- Hypothyroidism: TSH 9/25 in range, continue 75 mcg.
f/u after delivery.

conditions.label: Postpartum hemorrhage
conditions.note: After manual removal of retained placenta

reports.text: Transabdominal and transvaginal imaging of the postpartum pelvis. The uterus is enlarged as expected 4 days postpartum. The endometrial stripe is thin without echogenic material or internal vascularity to suggest retained products of conception. No intrauterine or adnexal fluid collection. Ovaries unremarkable. No free fluid in the pelvis.
reports.conclusion: Expected postpartum uterus. No retained products of conception. No fluid collection.

documents.title: Obstetrics Readmission Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY, OBSTETRICS (READMISSION)
Patient: Holly Barrett, 33 y/o, G4P4004
Admitted 05/31/2026. Discharged 06/02/2026.

Recent delivery: admitted here 05/27/2026 at 39w3d with an uncomplicated vaginal delivery; the placenta was retained and removed manually. Pre-delivery Hgb 12. Discharged home 05/29.

Reason for readmission: two days after going home she became lightheaded and steadily weaker and was brought back.

On arrival: BP 90/60, HR 120, RR 22, T 37.1 C. Abdomen soft, minimally tender. Bleeding no more than normal lochia. Hgb 7.0 (from 12 before delivery). Coags normal. Bedside FAST: no free fluid in the abdomen. After aggressive IV crystalloid, BP remained 85/55 with HR 128; managed as hemorrhagic shock.

Course: Transfused 3 units packed red cells. Afterward BP 110/68, HR 94, mentating normally. Pelvic ultrasound showed no retained products and no fluid collection. Post-transfusion Hgb 8.7 on 6/1; 8.9 on 6/2 and stable. No further bleeding beyond lochia during the stay.

PMH: hypothyroidism; iron deficiency anemia; PPH 06/2023 (atony) and 09/2024 (vaginal wall laceration).
Allergies: penicillin (rash); latex (contact dermatitis).

Discharge diagnoses: postpartum hemorrhage following manual removal of retained placenta; hemorrhagic shock, resolved with transfusion; acute blood loss anemia.
Discharge medications: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily; ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily; prenatal vitamin daily.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week for CBC. OB postpartum visit as scheduled. Return for heavy bleeding, fainting, or fever.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
TCM outreach. Readmitted 5/31-6/2 for hemorrhagic shock after 5/27 delivery (manual placenta removal), got 3 units. Summary received this morning.

Spoke with pt. Home, resting. Lightheaded once on standing yesterday, sat down and it passed. Bleeding light. Eating and drinking. Meds unchanged: levothyroxine, ferrous sulfate, prenatal.
Reviewed when to call 911 vs go to L&D: fainting, soaking a pad an hour, racing heart at rest, fever.
PCP visit Mon 6/8 10:40.

events.reason: Hospital follow-up, postpartum hemorrhage with shock

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit.

Delivered 5/27 (4th baby), retained placenta removed manually, home 5/29. Readmitted 5/31 lightheaded and weak, Hgb 7 from 12, BP stayed 85/55 HR 128 after fluids. FAST negative, pelvic US no retained tissue or collection. 3 u PRBC, Hgb 8.7 then 8.9. Home 6/2.

Today: up and around the house, tired. One lightheaded spell 6/2, none since. Lochia light. No fever. Eating ok. Mood "tired, not sad." Has help at home. Taking levothyroxine, ferrous sulfate, prenatal vitamin.

Exam: vitals as charted, no orthostatic symptoms on standing. Pale conjunctivae. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender, fundus below umbilicus. No calf tenderness or edema.
PHQ-9: 4.

A/P
1. Hemorrhagic shock from postpartum hemorrhage, resolved after transfusion. PPH resolved.
2. Acute blood loss anemia on chronic iron deficiency: CBC today. Continue ferrous sulfate 325 daily. CBC + iron studies in ~6 wks.
3. Hypothyroidism: continue 75 mcg; TSH at next visit.
4. Third PPH in her last three deliveries; OB aware and following.
TCM: RN contact 6/3, both admissions reviewed, meds reconciled.
